hints.title: Center Outward Expansion
hints.text: Every palindrome expands symmetrically from its center. In a string of length n, there are exactly 2n minus one possible centers.

hints.title: Bilateral Symmetry Growth Invariant
hints.text: Expanding two pointers outward while bounding characters match increments the valid palindrome count until encountering a mismatch.

hints.title: Center Expansion Counter Procedure
hints.text: Loop through all 2n minus one centers. Set left pointer to center divided by two and right pointer to left plus center modulo two. While within bounds and characters match, increment count and expand pointers outward. Return total count.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countSubstrings(self, s: str) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        count = 0
        for center in range(2 * n - 1):
            l = center // 2
            r = l + (center % 2)
            while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
                count += 1
                l -= 1
                r += 1
        return count
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every substring independently takes O(N^3) time due to repeated palindrome checks.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Expanding around centers checks each potential palindrome in O(N^2) total time while using strictly O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain both odd-length and even-length expansion centers and why expanding outward achieves optimal space.
